note: Owner-scoped tables not cleared by one or both deletion cascades. Reseeded 2026-08-11 after the Postgres cascade reached parity with the SQLite one (11 entries -> 6): Flag, Purchase, AgentActivity, TelemetryEvent and AgentMessage are now cleared on both. A deleted username is released for reuse (decision 2026-08-10), so anything left here is inheritable by the next registrant. Each remaining entry still needs the same decision: add it to BOTH cascades, or record here why the row must outlive its owner.

exempt.GroupShare: UNREVIEWED. Exposed 2026-08-24 when the scan was fixed to see CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, which it had been skipping — this table has been outside the check since 0033. It is reported as "missing in sqlite" only because the scan's cascade match is deliberately loose and found the name in methods/agent-misc.ts; no cascade clears it in EITHER provider. A group share names a key pattern one owner opened to a group, so a surviving row after that owner is deleted is an access grant with nobody behind it, and a released username makes it inheritable. Left for the developer because removing it changes what other members of that group can still read.
exempt.AgentUsageEventArchive: UNREVIEWED. Exposed 2026-08-24 by the same scan fix. The only delete against it is the timestamp-based prune in methods/usage.ts, which the loose cascade match counted; nothing clears it by owner in either provider. Left for the developer rather than fixed, because an archive of what was spent is the kind of record that may be meant to outlive the account — and if it is, that is a sentence to write here, not a delete to add.
